Thanks to @trukwava for the analysis — I agree with the conclusion that this needs a semantics call before code, and I want to add two facts that may help make that call, plus a concrete read on where the change would have to land.

Both `FIXME`s are still on master today, unchanged, at `packages/element/tests/zindex.test.tsx:1322` and `:1325`, so the issue is still live.

**1. There is no normalisation anywhere in `zindex.ts`.** I grepped the whole file (665 lines) for `normali` and got zero hits. So the reading that satisfies both `FIXME`s — children collapsing next to their frame as the frame moves — would not be restoring an existing invariant. It would introduce one, into the `moveOneLeft`/`moveOneRight` path specifically. That makes it a bigger decision than "make the failing test pass", which I think is worth being explicit about before anyone spends time on it.

**2. The frame-aware code lives on the other path.** The two public entry points do not share a helper:

```
moveOneLeft  (L626) -> shiftElementsByOne(...)              (L631)
moveOneRight (L634) -> shiftElementsByOne(...)              (L639)
moveAllLeft  (L642) -> shiftElementsAccountingForFrames(...) (L646)
moveAllRight (L654) -> shiftElementsAccountingForFrames(...) (L658)
```

`shiftElementsAccountingForFrames` is the only frame-aware implementation, and `shiftElementsByOne` has only partial frame handling of its own (`selectedFrames` at L361, the `containingFrame` check at L372). `shiftElementsByOne` also does its own contiguous-run splitting via `toContiguousGroups` (L355), which is what produces the independent one-slot moves in the denormalized case.

So there are really three options, and they are not equally cheap:

- **(a) Normalise on move** — satisfies both `FIXME`s, changes the currently-passing step 1, and adds an invariant `zindex.ts` does not have today. Largest change.
- **(b) Keep by-one semantics, correct the `FIXME` comments** — treat today's behaviour as intended and close the two `FIXME`s as wrong expectations. Smallest change, but it is a behaviour decision in the opposite direction from the issue.
- **(c) Make `moveOneLeft`/`moveOneRight` frame-aware** — treat frame plus all its children as one rigid unit. This contradicts step 1 as written, same as (a), but without normalising; the unit just moves.

Worth flagging for (a) and (c): `hasSameElementIds` guards were added to this area recently (#11485, "elements duplicated when moving frame children"), and they sit in `getTargetIndex` and `getTargetElementsMap`. Any change to how a frame's extent is computed has to keep those guards satisfied, otherwise the duplication bug comes back.

@dwelle — (a), (b) or (c)? I will implement whichever you pick behind the existing `DENORMALIZED FRAME ORDER` block, and run `yarn test:app packages/element/tests/zindex.test.tsx` plus the wider `packages/element` suite to check the `moveAll*` paths did not regress. I would rather spend the effort on the semantics you want than guess and have it bounce.

### Summary
The fix is right and minimal: both compact branches now reject anything that is not an ASCII digit instead of filtering it out. All valid compact forms still parse (`2015`, `201507`, `2015202`, `20150721`, `21`, `2140`, `214032`, `214032.142`), and the new tests would fail on the old code. The points below are non-blocking gaps around the edges of the change; the first one is pre-existing and worth tracking.

### Critical Issues
None found.

### Suggestions
| # | File | Line | Suggestion | Category |
|---|------|------|------------|----------|
| 1 | `graph/src/runtime/functions/temporal.rs` | 150, 243-262 | Pre-existing, but right next to this fix. Any string containing 'W' is routed to `parse_week_date` (L150) before the new check, so compact week dates (`2015W302`, listed next to `20150721` in TCK Temporal2) are validated only by `str::parse`: `+2015W+5` parses as 2015-W05. Also, L258 and L261 slice `rest[..2]` and `rest[2..]` at byte offsets without a char-boundary check, so a multi-byte character after the week number (for example `2015W3é`) looks like it can panic instead of returning an error (needs confirmation by running it). Suggest validating before slicing: `s[..w_pos]` is 4 ASCII digits and `rest` is 2 or 3 ASCII digits, the same check you added for the compact branches. Fine here or as a follow-up issue, but it should not stay untracked. | Robustness (pre-existing) |
| 2 | `graph/src/runtime/functions/temporal.rs` | 165, 169, 176, 289-298 | The description says the hyphenated and colon forms "already error" on junk. True for letters, but `str::parse` accepts a leading `+`: `date('+2015-+7-+21')` gives 2015-07-21 and `localtime('+12:+30')` gives 12:30, and `date('+2015')` now errors while `date('+2015-07')` does not. | 3 | `graph/src/runtime/functions/temporal.rs` | 284-285, 306-311 | The fraction is stripped before validation, so `localtime('214032.abc')` and `localtime('21:40:32.xyz')` still parse as 21:40:32, which is the same "junk silently dropped" bug. Check that the part after '.' is non-empty ASCII digits. | Correctness (adjacent) |
| 4 | `graph/src/runtime/functions/temporal.rs` | 157, 195, 306, 309 | After the new check, `digits_only` and `digits` are identical to `s`, and `digits_only` is allocated on every call, including the hyphenated path (the common one) where it is never used. | 5 | PR description | n/a | Please call out that these were previously accepted and now error: surrounding whitespace, a `T` prefix (`localtime('T1215')`), and a trailing `Z` or offset on compact forms (`localtime('214032Z')`, `localdatetime('20150721T121540Z')`). This looks consistent with the colon forms (which already reject `Z`) and with C (`Time_fromString` returns NULL for these). Whether Neo4j accepts a leading `T` is unconfirmed. | Behaviour change |
| 6 | `tests/flow/test_temporal.py` | `test_date_from_string`, `test_localtime_from_string` | The new tests are Rust unit tests only. Add a negative row or two (`2o15o7o21`, `xx123456yy`) to the flow tests so the error is seen end to end as a query error, as #3118 does, plus one non-ASCII case (for example `2015é07`) to guard against byte-slice panics. | Test coverage |

### What Looks Good
- Right scope: only the two compact branches change, and the hyphenated, colon and week forms are untouched, with tests saying so.
- Valid forms are preserved. I checked them against the existing flow tests (`test_date_from_string`, `test_localtime_from_string`, `test_localdatetime_from_string`) and the TCK Temporal2 strings; `214032.142` still works because the fraction is stripped first.

**Approve.** The suggestions are non-blocking; #1 deserves its own issue or follow-up.

Worth noting that the mechanism this issue asks for now exists in the codebase — it is just scoped to one element type.

#12064 (merged 2026-09-10) introduced exactly this split for the new `stickynote` element: `fontSizeMax` on the label is the user's ceiling, `fontSize` is a derived, fitted value, and `getStickyNoteLayout()` is a single pure function that wraps the text at the container width, searches for the largest font under the ceiling with a floor at 16, and only grows the container past its `baseHeight` once the text still overflows at that floor. Resize gestures are translated into explicit intents, so a width-only drag re-wraps while a proportional resize scales the ceiling instead of the text.

That is the "keep shape, change text size" behaviour @eldelacajita described, and it is already implemented, tested and shipping — but a rectangle or ellipse with bound text still uses the old grow-the-container path.

So the remaining ask here is narrower than when this was filed: expose the same fitting behaviour to ordinary bound-text containers, opt-in per element rather than as a new default. The "auto text size" toggle in the text settings proposed above would be a natural switch, with `fontSizeMax` as the value it captures.

The reason it still matters after #12064: mixed boards. In a flowchart, a decision diamond or a process box carries a label that should shrink to fit just like a note does, and those cannot be sticky notes without changing what the diagram means. Concretely, we generate teaching whiteboards where participants type into pre-placed, uniformly sized boxes; a note tool solves the free-form brainstorming surfaces, but the labelled shapes still drift out of alignment as soon as someone types one word too many.

## Code Review: fix: serialize schema-mutating commands through a single-writer election

### Summary
Moves the per-graph writer election out of `cmd_query.c` / `graphcontext.c` into the new `graph_write_queue.c`, routes `GRAPH.CONSTRAINT` CREATE/DROP through it as queued tasks, and rejects `GRAPH.EFFECT` unless the context is REPLICATED or LOADING. The election itself is a faithful lift of the existing code, and the constraint task's unblock/free handling is correct on every branch I traced (graph missing, queue full, task executed). The gaps are that the constraint task re-resolves the graph by name, that the regression test can pass vacuously, and that the queue-full branch of `_query` (which this PR rewrites) appears to crash.

### Critical Issues
| # | File | Line | Issue | Severity |
|---|------|------|-------|----------|
| 1 | `src/commands/cmd_constraint.c` | 662-707 (re-lookups at ~262-273 and ~458-470) | **The queued task re-resolves the graph by name, so it may run under the wrong graph's election token.** `Async_Constraint_Op` takes the election on the `gc` it looked up, but the task then calls `GraphContext_Retrieve(key)` again inside `_Constraint_Create/_Drop` and never checks it got the same `gc`. The wait in the queue can be long (up to 1024 tasks); if `GRAPH.DELETE`, `DEL`/`RENAME`/`RESTORE` or an offload+reload swaps the key's GraphContext in that window, the constraint mutates gc2 while holding gc1's token, so gc2's own writers are not serialized with it (the very race this PR fixes). For CREATE it can also silently re-create a deleted graph. Fix: carry the looked-up `gc` (with its ref) in `GraphConstraintCtx` and pass it to `_Constraint_Create/_Drop` on the async path (the sync AOF/replica path keeps retrieving by name), or at minimum compare pointers and reply with an error on mismatch. Reachability is needs confirmation (read from code, not run). | 🔴 Critical |
| 2 | `src/commands/cmd_query.c` | `_DelegateQuery` ~366-393; `cleanup` ~572-601 | **Queue-full path dereferences a NULL QueryCtx (pre-existing, but on a path this PR rewrites).** `_DelegateQuery` calls `QueryCtx_RemoveFromTLS()` and untracks the CommandCtx before submitting. When `GraphContext_SubmitWrite` returns false, `_query` sets the error and jumps to `cleanup`, where `ErrorCtx_EmitException()` calls `QueryCtx_GetRedisModuleCtx()`, which reads the now-NULL TLS QueryCtx (ASSERT in debug, NULL deref in release). `QueryCtx_Free()` below it has the same problem, and the second `Globals_UntrackCommandCtx` can trip its assert; the detached QueryCtx and `gq_ctx` also appear to be leaked. So once 1024 writes are pending on one graph, the next `GRAPH.QUERY` write would take the server down instead of returning `EMSG_WRITE_QUEUE_FULL`. The new constraint branch handles queue-full correctly, the query branch does not. Fix: on failure undo what `_DelegateQuery` did (restore the TLS QueryCtx, re-track the CommandCtx, restore thread/stage) and free `gq_ctx` before `goto cleanup`; add a test with a small or configurable queue cap. Needs confirmation (no test hits it, I did not run it). | 🔴 Critical (pre-existing) |

### Suggestions
| # | File | Line | Suggestion | Category |
|---|------|------|------------|----------|
| 1 | `tests/flow/test_constraint.py` | ~640-704 | 🟡 **The regression test can pass vacuously** (agreeing with CodeRabbit). Both workers swallow every `ResponseError`, so if every `CONSTRAINT CREATE` failed the test would still pass, and detecting the original bug depends on the race crashing the server. The wait-for-enforcement loop also silently proceeds after 5s. Fix: count successes and assert they equal the expected total (labels are unique, so no legitimate failures), assert `len(list_constraints(g))` matches, and assert `pending == []` after the wait. Also add DROP-vs-query, `GRAPH.CONSTRAINT DROP` on a missing graph (covers the new `gc == NULL` branch) and the queue-full case. The test is skipped under SANITIZER/VALGRIND, exactly where this race would show up; a reduced version there would help. | Testing |
| 2 | `src/graph/graph_write_queue.h` | 10-22 | 🟡 The header says every command that mutates a graph must flow through this election, but not every writer does: `GRAPH.QUERY` writes inside MULTI/EXEC (and replicated or loading ones) run `_ExecuteQuery` directly on the main thread, and the sync AOF/replica paths of `GRAPH.CONSTRAINT` / `GRAPH.EFFECT` are outside the election. Overlap looks reachable on a writable replica or a demoted master with in-flight writer-thread writes (needs confirmation). Suggest softening the claim and filing a follow-up. | Correctness / scope |
| 3 | `src/commands/cmd_constraint.c` | ~349-368, 484-503, 704-705 | 🟡 Stale or inaccurate comments: the closing comment of `Async_Constraint_Op` says `GraphContext_SubmitWrite` holds its own ref across the queued task, but per my read that ref is released when it returns, so the queued task owns no ref of its own (ties into Critical #1). The `_Constraint_CreatePrecheck` rationale about a concurrent write query's in-flight reservation no longer applies on the async path. | Maintainability |
| 4 | `src/graph/graphcontext.h`, `src/commands/cmd_constraint.c` | ~178-190; ~698 | 🔵 `GraphContext_EnqueueWriteQuery/DequeueWriteQuery` are still public with `void*` although the queue now holds `WriteTask*`; make them static in `graph_write_queue.c`. The literal `"Graph write queue is full"` should be `EMSG_WRITE_QUEUE_FULL` as the query path uses. Each write now also pays an extra `rm_malloc/rm_free` for the `WriteTask`; storing it inline in the `CircularBuffer` would avoid that. | Nit |
| 5 | `src/commands/cmd_effect.c` | 31-44 | 🟡 Compatibility: any ordinary client calling `GRAPH.EFFECT` now gets an error, so tooling that replays a replication/AOF stream through a normal connection will break. Please call this out in the PR description (currently only the auto-generated summary) and the release notes. | Docs |

### What Looks Good
- Lifting the election into one module removes the `extern enter_writer_loop` back-reference from `graphcontext.c`, and the ref / enqueue / CAS / drain / unref ordering matches the old behaviour. The defrag hand-off works for constraint tasks unchanged.
- Constraint ownership is clean: exactly one `UnblockClient` and one `GraphConstraintCtx_Free` on all three branches, and `ctx` is never touched after hand-off.
- The `GRAPH.EFFECT` gate uses the same REPLICATED/LOADING pair as the dispatcher and `Graph_Constraint`, sits before any state access, and removes the client-reachable path into `Effects_Apply`. `test34_effect_rejected_from_client` is deterministic.

### Verdict
Request Changes (small): please address Critical #1 and tighten the test (Suggestion #1). Critical #2 is pre-existing but sits in code this PR rewrites and takes the server down, so it is worth fixing here or in an immediate follow-up. The rest can be follow-ups.

## Code Review: fix: pattern predicates in WITH ... WHERE refer to pre-projection variables (#3061)

### Summary
Pattern predicates in `WITH ... WHERE` bound a fresh `n` because `bind_graph` looks names up in the current scope only, so `WITH n.v AS k WHERE (n)-->()` tested whether any node had an out-edge. The PR extracts the existing pattern-comprehension pre-copy into `import_parent_names`, applies it to pattern predicates, and for a renamed variable (`WITH n AS m`) enters it under the pattern's name for the duration of the bind. Behaviour is unchanged where parent scope is not visible (early return on `!use_parent_scope`). I checked the five test cases by hand against the data and the expected values are right; cases 1, 2 and 4 fail without the fix.

### Critical Issues
None found.

### Suggestions
| # | File | Line | Suggestion | Category |
|---|------|------|-----------|----------|
| 1 | `graph/src/planner/binder.rs` | 1886, 2071, 2125-2150 | The transient alias lives in `current_env`, which is also the id allocator (`fresh_var` and `resolve_name` use `env.len()`), and the planner mints at `scope_vars[scope].len()` (also for the inline OR/NOT pattern path, `planner/mod.rs` 1590-1619). While the alias exists the pattern's `_anon` variables get ids shifted by one; after removal the table has a gap. The same gap already arises for named pattern-locals removed by `retain`, so this is likely not a regression, but none of the five cases exercises the non-extractable path. Add `MATCH (n) WITH n AS m WHERE (n)-->(:B) OR m.v = 0 RETURN m.v ORDER BY m.v` and a query with two predicates on the same renamed variable. Needs confirmation. | Tests / Correctness |
| 2 | `graph/src/planner/binder.rs` | 1209-1216 | For an aggregating or DISTINCT WITH, the check "ORDER BY cannot reference variables not projected" runs before the filter is bound. After this change a pattern predicate in WHERE over a non-projected variable (`MATCH (n) WITH count(n) AS c WHERE (n)-->() RETURN c`) copies `n` from a scope the aggregation has already collapsed; before, it silently bound a fresh `n`. Please pin the intended behaviour (error, as for the scalar form `WHERE n.v > 0`, or a defined result) with a test. Needs confirmation. | Correctness |
| 3 | `tests/flow/test_with_clause.py` | 390-406 | The description names ORDER BY as a visible-parent-scope context, but only WHERE is tested. Add an ORDER BY pattern comprehension on a pre-projection variable, a relationship variable from the parent (`(n)-[r]->()`), and the shadowing case `WITH n AS m, 1 AS n WHERE (n)-->()` (the current-env name wins, so this should error). | Tests |
| 4 | `graph/src/planner/binder.rs` | 1853-1890, 2043-2074 | The snapshot, `retain`, remove-alias sequence is now duplicated at two call sites. A small helper that wraps "import, bind, clean up" would keep them in step. | Maintainability |

- One shared helper instead of two diverging copies; the pattern-comprehension path keeps its old behaviour for copied names (the new `!contains_key` check after `resolve_name` means only genuinely renamed entries are aliased).

- Diff against the merge-base is 2 files, no unrelated changes.

| # | File | Line | Suggestion | Category |
|---|------|------|------------|----------|

| 5 | `src/module.c` | 164-168 | 🟡 Behaviour change worth a note in the PR/release notes: Redis's `useDisklessLoad()` skips diskless load unless all module datatypes declare they handle IO errors. Before this PR a FalkorDB replica logged "Skipping diskless-load..." and fell back to disk; now `repl-diskless-load on-empty-db` really activates for FalkorDB. That is the intended feature, but it deserves a test (see #1). | Behaviour change |

- The sticky flag lives on the per-load, calloc'd `SerializerIO`, so there is no reset or thread-safety concern.

- The CRC re-framing trick in the test, with its sanity check, is neat.

Request Changes: fix the graphmeta NULL crash and the `RdbLoadGraphContext_latest` contract (return NULL, tear down inside), and add tests that truncate mid-decode.

Repro'd, root-caused and opened a fix: #12029.

Two compounding defects: (1) `ColorInput` auto-focused the hex input on every `activeSection` change — since the section atom is shared across picker instances, a stale `"hex"` leftover re-focused the field on reopen; (2) the hex field's `onKeyDown` stopped propagation unconditionally, so `I`/`Alt` were typed into the input instead of toggling the eyedropper (`i` isn't even a hex character, so the value just corrupted).

Fix: hex focuses only when deliberately active; the picker derives its section fresh on mount; and the hex field handles `I`/`Alt` itself with the picker's exact semantics, so the advertised shortcut works from every section. The focused-hex regression test fails on master (verified) and passes with the fix; all 4 color-picker suites stay green.

[P1] Preserve unreadable stored scenes instead of treating them as empty
Location: [firebase.ts:118–126](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/cf98274e50e24b6f1ebcc8ae3b2f842320166f87/excalidraw-app/data/firebase.ts#L118-L126), consumed by [saveToFirebase:229–246](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/cf98274e50e24b6f1ebcc8ae3b2f842320166f87/excalidraw-app/data/firebase.ts#L229-L246).

A successful decryption does not establish that an unreadable payload contains no recoverable drawing data. Returning [] on JSON parse failure removes the distinction between corruption and a valid empty room. Loading now reports success with an empty scene; the next save reconciles against that empty array and updates the same Firestore document, destroying its original ciphertext without retaining a recovery copy or requiring an explicit reset.

I reproduced this using a stored plaintext beginning [{"id":"recoverable-rectangle","type":"rectangle","x":100 and a new local rectangle. At the reviewed head, loadFromFirebase returned []; saveToFirebase performed one transaction update containing only the new rectangle. Against the exact merge base, both operations rejected with SyntaxError and there were zero updates. Firestore and encryption were mocked at their boundaries; the production decrypt/parse, restore, reconciliation and save control flow ran unchanged. No real room was modified.

The code explicitly intends this as self-healing, but it makes a recoverable parse failure destructive. Wrong-key/tampered-ciphertext errors still throw; this finding concerns plaintext that authenticated successfully but cannot be interpreted. It is not an unauthenticated attack claim.

Correction: retain a distinct unreadable-scene result and block replacement of that stored document until recovery/reset is explicit, or preserve the original ciphertext in a recovery record before resetting. A genuinely empty array should remain a valid scene. Add load/save regressions asserting that parse failures and unexpected top-level shapes cannot silently replace existing storage.

[P2] Validate SCENE_INIT.payload.elements before marking the room initialized
Location: [Collab.tsx:605–623](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/cf98274e50e24b6f1ebcc8ae3b2f842320166f87/excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx#L605-L623), interacting with [restore.ts:1108–1114](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/cf98274e50e24b6f1ebcc8ae3b2f842320166f87/packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts#L1108-L1114).

The new INIT guard checks only that payload is an object. While joining an existing room, send:

{ "type": "SCENE_INIT", "payload": { "elements": {} } }

initializeRoom({fetchScene:false}) marks the socket initialized and clears its fallback timer. The new restoreElements guard converts the invalid element container to [], so no exception reaches the new Firebase fallback. The scene promise resolves with an empty scene, and a later valid INIT is ignored because initialization has already completed.

The regression invokes the actual registered client-broadcast handler with mocked transport/decryption, then sends a valid INIT containing a rectangle. The head returns {elements:[],scrollToContent:true} and ignores that rectangle. Adding only !Array.isArray(decryptedData.payload.elements) to the guard makes the same test pass. The temporary control was reverted afterward.

This is incomplete hardening, not a claim that this payload previously worked: the exact base throws items.reduce is not a function on the same input. The PR replaces that failure with silent empty initialization instead of its stated behavior of ignoring malformed INIT while preserving later initialization. Preconditions are a malformed message from a room participant with access to the room key.

Correction: reject invalid element containers before changing initialization state. Preserve the timer and allow a later valid INIT; a valid elements: [] must still initialize an intentionally empty room. Test missing, object, string and null element containers as well as a subsequent valid message.
